stem: Priya heats a pot of water on a stove in her kitchen. The water at the bottom of the pot is heated first. Which statement correctly describes how the rest of the water becomes hot?

options.text: The heated water expands, becomes lighter and rises, while cooler water moves down to take its place.
The heated water becomes heavier and sinks, pushing the cooler water up to the top.
Heat travels through the water only when the water starts boiling and bubbles appear.
The warm water stays at the bottom, and the rest of the pot heats up without any water moving.

teacher.key_rationale: Heating water from below causes the lower layer to expand, decrease in density, and rise; cooler denser water sinks to replace it, setting up a convection current. Option A states this correctly. Options B, C and D reflect common misconceptions: reversal of the rise/sink relationship, the idea that convection needs boiling, and the idea that heat spreads without fluid movement.
